subject: Acme - Rerank model validation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.com>, Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - post-call recap & sample data request

Hi Joe and Sofia —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation on your reranking pain points and the long-tail quality issues you see in search results. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal: improve top-K relevance for search/retrieval use cases (focus NDCG@10 and MRR for product/FAQ queries).
- Baseline: you're currently using an in-house BM25 + shallow reranker with noisy signals around entity-rich queries.
- What we’ll do next: run a focused eval comparing Redwood-candidates vs your baseline on the sample prompt set you provide, report NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR, and propose an A/B plan for production validation.

Action items:
1) Please send a ~2k sample of anonymized queries + golden labels (or let us pull via the S3 link you shared). If you prefer, a CSV with columns: query, doc_id, label is fine.
2) We'll run an initial sweep across 3 candidate rerank models (see recommended models below) and share NDCG/MRR output + error analysis within 48 business hours.
3) If results look promising, propose an A/B that runs 2 weeks with telemetry (CTR, click-through relevance, business KPI).

Recommended starting models (high-level):
- redwood/rerank-1.0 (dense+cross-attention, standard FP16)
- redwood/rerank-2.0-quant (8-bit optimized for latency)
- redwood/ensemble-rerank-v1 (hybrid dense + lightweight cross-ranker)

I'll attach a small prompt set template and a stub for the results file so you know the format we’ll return.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: prompt_set_v3.jsonl (template), acme_rerank_benchmarks.md (runbook)

From: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap & sample data request

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick recap. We're attaching a trimmed sample (anonymized) of ~2,200 queries as requested; included columns are query, doc_id, label. A couple clarifications:

- We only have implicit feedback for many items (clicks). For a ~300 subset we have human relevance labels; please use that for the gold set and treat clicks as noisy labels.
- For PII reasons we can't share raw doc text; we can share doc_id and a retrieval snapshot. If you need more context, we can coordinate with Data Engineering to provide a temporary view.

Also: curious about the recommended models — can you say which one tends to be best for entity-rich queries? Latency is important; anything above 120ms tail is a hard stop for some flows.

Thanks,
Joe
Joe Smith | Head of Search, Acme Corp
joe.smith@acme.com

Attachments: acme_sample_queries_2200.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.com>, Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap & sample data request

Joe —

Appreciate the sample, that’s perfect. Quick answers up front:

- Entity-rich queries: the ensemble-rerank-v1 tends to handle entity disambiguation best because it blends a dense retriever signal with a tighter cross-attention reranker. In our internal tests it reduced entity-related inversions by ~18% relative to rerank-1.0 on similar datasets.
- Latency: rerank-2.0-quant is the best latency/quality tradeoff (8-bit kernels); typical p95 is ~85–110ms on the instance types we recommend. We’ll include tail latency breakdowns in the report.

We ran the initial sweep against your gold subset (n=300) to get early signals — results attached and summarized below. Note: this is a small sample so treat as indicative rather than definitive. Full CSV attached: ndcg_mrr_results_q2.csv

Summary (gold subset, n=300):
- Baseline (BM25+shallow): NDCG@10 = 0.412, MRR = 0.346
- redwood/rerank-1.0: NDCG@10 = 0.572, MRR = 0.498
- redwood/rerank-2.0-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.548, MRR = 0.481
- redwood/ensemble-rerank-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.605, MRR = 0.523

Initial observations:
- Ensemble shows strongest gains on entity-heavy and multi-intent queries.
- Quantized model (2.0-quant) retains most quality while improving latency; however, we saw small regressions on very long queries (>120 tokens). We flagged a set of ~18 queries for further error analysis (included in the CSV).

Proposed A/B plan:
- A/B variants: Control = Baseline pipeline; Variant A = rerank-1.0; Variant B = ensemble-rerank-v1 (recommended).
- Metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), MRR, CTR uplift, p95 latency, failure rate.
- Sample size & duration: to detect a 2.5% NDCG uplift at 95% CI we estimate ~250k queries per arm; we recommend a 2-week run across peak & off-peak to capture variance.
- Rollout: start with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% if telemetry is healthy. Automatic rollback thresholds for latency or error spikes.

Next steps from us (Rishi & Monica are looped for ops and CS):
- If you approve, we’ll prepare the A/B config and a runbook (Doc link).
- We’ll also share a short prompt-set file used for the eval (attached: prompt_set_v3.jsonl) and the full benchmark writeup (acme_rerank_benchmarks.md).

Open question: do you want us to include a hybrid fallback that serves rerank-2.0-quant at high load and ensemble at normal load (automated fallback by policy)? That can give you predictable latency while preserving quality when load allows.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: ndcg_mrr_results_q2.csv, prompt_set_v3.jsonl, acme_rerank_benchmarks.md

From: Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap & sample data request

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and the numbers look promising. A couple quick items before we kick off A/B:

- Can you add expected p95 tail latency for the ensemble at the recommended instance size and the memory footprint for the quantized variant? We need these for procurement/infra sizing.
- Please add the exact rollback thresholds (we prefer numeric thresholds in the runbook).

We’re happy to proceed with the A/B plan you suggested. Can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff early next week to align on monitoring dashboards and the automation for rollback? Joe and I are available Mon/Tue mornings (PDT).

Sofia
Sofia Lopez | Senior Product Manager, Search — Acme Corp
sofia.lopez@acme.com
